prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "monitoring", with the standing line "A pulled metrics stack that samples the dalleserver host every few seconds and draws it as one live dashboard." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A wide horizontal diagram on one machine. At left, the dalleserver process with a small open port hatch labelled as its metrics endpoint; below it a second box, Node Exporter, reading the machine's processor and memory. Both are targets. From Prometheus, drawn centre as a boxy container holding a stack of stacked time-slices like sediment, two arrows reach LEFTWARD to the two targets and draw samples back — the arrowheads returning into the store show Prometheus pulling, not the apps pushing. From the store, a single query arrow runs rightward into Grafana, a lighter container; from Grafana one arrow leaves the machine outward to a browser at the public address. A dotted boundary encloses all three containers, marking them as one composed group.

Magnified circles set beside it show A magnified circle on the scrape clock, showing one sample landing every fifteen seconds into the store. A magnified circle on the store's oldest edge, showing samples ageing out at thirty days. A magnified circle on the configuration file that names the two scrape targets. A magnified circle on the Grafana front door showing the admin login and the Prometheus data source it is pointed at.

Colour is used so that Warm red marks errors, OpenAI errors and timeouts. Green marks healthy service state and resource lines. Blue marks the movement of scraped samples and queries. Grey marks the containers themselves.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 15-second scrape interval; 30-day retention, 720 hours; 2 scrape targets; 8 dashboard panels; 5-minute rate window; 6-hour default view; 30-second refresh; 3 containers.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: /metrics on the port hatch of dalleserver; prometheus.yml on the configuration inset; docker-compose.yml on the dotted container boundary; dalleserver_up on the Service Status study; dalleserver_errors_total on the Total Errors study; metrics.dalledress.io on the browser; Prometheus, Node Exporter and Grafana each on their own container; Service Status, Total Errors, OpenAI Requests, OpenAI Errors, CPU Usage, Memory Usage, OpenAI Request Rate and Error Rate each on their own panel.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: dalleserver, /metrics, Node Exporter, scrape target, Prometheus, time-series store, Grafana, query, pulls samples, one host prometheus.yml, docker-compose.yml, scrape interval, data source, admin login Service Status, Total Errors, OpenAI Requests, OpenAI Errors, CPU Usage, Memory Usage Dalleserver Production Metrics, OpenAI Request Rate, Error Rate, timeouts, metrics.dalledress.io start, follow logs, update images, restart, stop, back up Grafana

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Prometheus reaches out; nothing is pushed in; Node Exporter reports the machine, not the app; Grafana reads only what Prometheus already stored. One file names both scrape targets; Grafana is pointed at Prometheus by URL. Counters show totals; rates show recent movement. Dashboard is imported from a JSON model; dalleserver_up above zero means trouble.
